### Quickstart with Peekaboo CLI

Source: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/main/skills/peekaboo/SKILL.md

Basic commands to get started with Peekaboo, including checking permissions, listing applications, taking a screenshot, clicking an element, and typing text.

```bash
peekaboo permissions
peekaboo list apps --json
peekaboo see --annotate --path /tmp/peekaboo-see.png
peekaboo click --on B1
peekaboo type "Hello" --return
```

### Install and run the node host

Source: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/main/docs/plugins/google-meet.md

Install the Google Meet plugin and start the node host within the VM.

```bash
openclaw plugins install npm:@openclaw/google-meet
openclaw node run --host <gateway-host> --port 18789 --display-name parallels-macos
```

Source: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/main/docs/help/faq-first-run.md

```bash
curl -fsSL --proto '=https' --tlsv1.2 https://openclaw.ai/install.sh | bash -s -- --install-method git
curl -fsSL --proto '=https' --tlsv1.2 https://openclaw.ai/install.sh | bash -s -- --install-method npm
```

### Run OpenClaw setup commands

Source: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/main/docs/web/tui.md

Commands for starting the setup assistant interactively or executing specific configuration tasks.

```bash
openclaw setup                       # start interactively
openclaw setup -m "status"           # run one request and exit
openclaw setup -m "set default model openai/gpt-5.2" --yes   # apply a config write
```

```bash

litellm --model claude-opus-4-6
```

```bash
export LITELLM_API_KEY="your-litellm-key"
openclaw
```

### Define Thread Start Parameters

Source: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/main/test/fixtures/agents/prompt-snapshots/codex-runtime-happy-path/telegram-direct-codex-message-tool.md

Specifies the initial configuration, dynamic tools, and sandbox environment for starting a new OpenClaw thread.

```json
{
  "approvalPolicy": "never",
  "approvalsReviewer": "user",
  "config": {
    "code_mode.direct_only_tool_namespaces": ["openclaw_direct"],
    "features.apply_patch_streaming_events": true,
    "features.code_mode": true,
    "features.code_mode_only": false,
    "features.goals": false,
    "features.standalone_web_search": false,
    "web_search": "cached"
  },
  "cwd": "/tmp/openclaw-happy-path/workspace",
  "developerInstructions": "<see Reconstructed Model-Bound Prompt Layers>",
  "dynamicTools": [
    "agents_list",
    "message",
    "sessions_spawn",
    "automations",
    "gateway",
    "nodes",
    "session_status",
    "sessions_history",
    "sessions_list",
    "sessions_search",
    "sessions_send",
    "subagents",
    "tts",
    "web_fetch",
    "web_search",
    "sessions_yield"
  ],
  "experimentalRawEvents": true,
  "model": "gpt-5.5",
  "personality": "none",
  "sandbox": "danger-full-access",
  "serviceName": "OpenClaw"
}
```

--------------------------------

### GET /__openclaw__/assistant-media

Source: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/main/docs/web/control-ui.md

Retrieves metadata for assistant local-media previews, providing a short-lived media ticket for secure media rendering.

```APIDOC
## GET /__openclaw__/assistant-media

### Description
Checks availability of assistant local-media and returns a short-lived mediaTicket for secure access to the media file.

### Method
GET

### Endpoint
/__openclaw__/assistant-media

### Parameters
#### Query Parameters
- **meta** (integer) - Required - Must be set to 1.
- **source** (string) - Required - The path to the media source.
```

--------------------------------

### Turn Start Parameters JSON

Source: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/main/test/fixtures/agents/prompt-snapshots/codex-runtime-happy-path/telegram-heartbeat-codex-tool.md

Configuration object defining the agent's operating mode, workspace context, and behavioral instructions for a heartbeat turn.

```json
{
  "approvalPolicy": "never",
  "approvalsReviewer": "user",
  "collaborationMode": {
    "mode": "default",
    "settings": {
      "developer_instructions": "This is an OpenClaw heartbeat turn. Apply these instructions only to this heartbeat wake; ordinary chat turns should stay in Codex Default mode.\n\nWhen you are ready to end the heartbeat, prefer the structured `heartbeat_respond` tool so OpenClaw can record the wake outcome and notification decision. If `heartbeat_respond` is not already available and `tool_search` is available, search for `heartbeat_respond`, load it, then call it. Use `notify=false` when nothing should visibly interrupt the user.\n\n### Heartbeats\n\nHeartbeat = useful proactive progress, not chatter. Wake, orient, use the provided monitor scratch, act.\nAssigned/ongoing work: pursue spirit with judgment. Quiet check counts only if real blocker/urgent interruption.\nNo rote loops; orientation != accomplishment. Prefer action/silent progress.\nNever repetitive \"same/no change/still\" updates.\nInterrupt only for meaningful development/result/blocker/decision/time risk. Unchanged: work, change approach, dig deeper, or silence.\n\n## OpenClaw Agent Soul\n\nOpenClaw loaded these workspace instruction files from the active agent workspace. They are the canonical definitions of who you are, how you think and work, and the human you work alongside. Internalize and follow them accordingly.\n\n### /tmp/openclaw-happy-path/workspace/IDENTITY.md\n\n<IDENTITY.md contents will be here>\n\n### /tmp/openclaw-happy-path/workspace/SOUL.md\n\n<SOUL.md contents will be here>\n\n### /tmp/openclaw-happy-path/workspace/USER.md\n\n<USER.md contents will be here>",
      "model": "gpt-5.5",
      "reasoning_effort": "medium"
    }
  },
  "cwd": "/tmp/openclaw-happy-path/workspace",
  "effort": "medium",
  "input": [
    {
      "text": "<see Reconstructed Model-Bound Prompt Layers>",
      "text_elements": [],
      "type": "text"
    }
  ],
  "model": "gpt-5.5",
  "personality": "none",
  "sandboxPolicy": {
    "type": "dangerFullAccess"
  },
  "threadId": "thread-telegram-heartbeat-codex-tool"
}
```

### Turn Start JSON Configuration

Source: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/main/test/fixtures/agents/prompt-snapshots/codex-runtime-happy-path/telegram-direct-codex-message-tool.md

Configuration object defining the agent's operational mode, workspace path, and sandbox access level for a specific thread.

```json
{
  "approvalPolicy": "never",
  "approvalsReviewer": "user",
  "collaborationMode": {
    "mode": "default",
    "settings": {
      "developer_instructions": "# Collaboration Mode: Default\n\nYou are now in Default mode. Any previous instructions for other modes (e.g. Plan mode) are no longer active.\n\nYour active mode changes only when new developer instructions with a different `<collaboration_mode>...</collaboration_mode>` change it; user requests or tool descriptions do not change mode by themselves. Known mode names are Default and Plan.\n\n## request_user_input availability\n\nUse the `request_user_input` tool only when it is listed in the available tools for this turn.\n\nIn Default mode, strongly prefer making reasonable assumptions and executing the user's request rather than stopping to ask questions. If you absolutely must ask a question because the answer cannot be discovered from local context and a reasonable assumption would be risky, ask the user directly with a concise plain-text question. Never write a multiple choice question as a textual assistant message.\n\n## OpenClaw Agent Soul\n\nOpenClaw loaded these workspace instruction files from the active agent workspace. They are the canonical definitions of who you are, how you think and work, and the human you work alongside. Internalize and follow them accordingly.\n\n### /tmp/openclaw-happy-path/workspace/IDENTITY.md\n\n<IDENTITY.md contents will be here>\n\n### /tmp/openclaw-happy-path/workspace/SOUL.md\n\n<SOUL.md contents will be here>\n\n### /tmp/openclaw-happy-path/workspace/USER.md\n\n<USER.md contents will be here>",
      "model": "gpt-5.5",
      "reasoning_effort": "medium"
    }
  },
  "cwd": "/tmp/openclaw-happy-path/workspace",
  "effort": "medium",
  "input": [
    {
      "text": "<see Reconstructed Model-Bound Prompt Layers>",
      "text_elements": [],
      "type": "text"
    }
  ],
  "model": "gpt-5.5",
  "personality": "none",
  "sandboxPolicy": {
    "type": "dangerFullAccess"
  },
  "threadId": "thread-telegram-direct-codex-message-tool"
}
```

### TTS configuration examples

Source: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/main/docs/plugins/voice-call.md

Examples demonstrating core TTS setup, plugin-specific overrides, and model configuration.

```json5
{
  tts: {
    provider: "openai",
    providers: {
      openai: { speakerVoice: "alloy" },
    },
  },
}
```

```json5
{
  plugins: {
    entries: {
      "voice-call": {
        config: {
          tts: {
            provider: "elevenlabs",
            providers: {
              elevenlabs: {
                apiKey: "elevenlabs_key",
                speakerVoiceId: "pMsXgVXv3BLzUgSXRplE",
                modelId: "eleven_multilingual_v2",
              },
            },
          },
        },
      },
    },
  },
}
```

```json5
{
  plugins: {
    entries: {
      "voice-call": {
        config: {
          tts: {
            providers: {
              openai: {
                model: "gpt-4o-mini-tts",
                speakerVoice: "marin",
              },
            },
          },
        },
      },
    },
  },
}
```

--------------------------------

### GET /avatar/<agentId>

Source: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/main/docs/web/control-ui.md

Retrieves the avatar image or metadata for a specific agent. Requires a gateway token as a bearer header when gateway authentication is enabled.

```APIDOC
## GET /avatar/<agentId>

### Description
Retrieves the avatar image for the specified agent. Optionally returns metadata if the meta query parameter is set.

### Method
GET

### Endpoint
/avatar/<agentId>

### Parameters
#### Path Parameters
- **agentId** (string) - Required - The unique identifier of the agent.

#### Query Parameters
- **meta** (integer) - Optional - If set to 1, returns avatar metadata instead of the image.
```

### Example stdin for Install Policy

Source: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/main/docs/tools/skills-config.md

Represents the JSON object sent to the policy command via stdin during an installation request.

```json
{
  "protocolVersion": 1,
  "openclawVersion": "2026.6.1",
  "targetType": "skill",
  "targetName": "weather",
  "sourcePath": "/var/folders/.../openclaw-skill-clawhub/root",
  "sourcePathKind": "directory",
  "source": {
    "kind": "clawhub",
    "authority": "openclaw",
    "mutable": false,
    "network": true
  },
  "origin": {
    "type": "clawhub",
    "registry": "https://clawhub.openclaw.ai",
    "slug": "weather",
    "version": "1.0.0"
  },
  "request": {
    "kind": "skill-install",
    "mode": "install",
    "requestedSpecifier": "clawhub:weather@1.0.0"
  },
  "skill": {
    "installId": "clawhub"
  }
}
```

### Configure Pinned npm Installation

Source: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/main/docs/plugins/sdk-setup.md

Example of specifying a pinned npm package version and integrity hash for plugin installation.

```json
{
  "openclaw": {
    "install": {
      "npmSpec": "@wecom/wecom-openclaw-plugin@1.2.3",
      "expectedIntegrity": "sha512-REPLACE_WITH_NPM_DIST_INTEGRITY",
      "defaultChoice": "npm"
    }
  }
}
```

### Non-interactive setup

Source: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/main/docs/providers/deepseek.md

Perform a headless or scripted onboarding setup by passing all configuration flags directly.

```bash
openclaw onboard --non-interactive \
  --mode local \
  --auth-choice deepseek-api-key \
  --deepseek-api-key "$DEEPSEEK_API_KEY" \
  --skip-health \
  --accept-risk
```

--------------------------------

### Example Project Environment File

Source: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/main/scripts/clawdock/README.md

Shows a typical `<project>/.env` file, configuring Docker infrastructure settings like image name, ports, and gateway token.

```bash
OPENCLAW_CONFIG_DIR=/Users/you/.openclaw
OPENCLAW_WORKSPACE_DIR=/Users/you/.openclaw/workspace
OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_PORT=18789
OPENCLAW_BRIDGE_PORT=18790
OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_BIND=lan
OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_TOKEN=<generated-by-docker-setup>
OPENCLAW_AUTH_PROFILE_SECRET_DIR=/Users/you/.openclaw-auth-profile-secrets
OPENCLAW_IMAGE=openclaw:local
```

--------------------------------

### Run interactive onboarding

Source: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/main/docs/providers/longcat.md

Start the interactive onboarding process to configure the LongCat API key.

```bash
openclaw onboard --auth-choice longcat-api-key
```

--------------------------------

### Run Onboarding for Standard Plan

Source: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/main/docs/providers/qwen.md

Execute the onboarding command to authenticate with the Standard pay-as-you-go endpoint.

```bash
openclaw onboard --auth-choice qwen-standard-api-key
```

```bash
openclaw onboard --auth-choice qwen-standard-api-key-cn
```

--------------------------------

### mcporter Quick Start Commands

Source: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/main/skills/mcporter/SKILL.md

Basic commands to quickly get started with `mcporter` for listing servers and making simple tool calls.

```bash
mcporter list
```

```bash
mcporter list <server> --schema
```

```bash
mcporter call <server.tool> key=value
```

--------------------------------

### Run onboarding for Xiaomi

Source: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/main/docs/providers/xiaomi.md

Execute the onboarding process using either pay-as-you-go or Token Plan authentication methods.

```bash
openclaw onboard --auth-choice xiaomi-api-key
```

```bash
openclaw onboard --auth-choice xiaomi-token-plan-sgp
```

```bash
openclaw onboard --auth-choice xiaomi-api-key --xiaomi-api-key "$XIAOMI_API_KEY"
openclaw onboard --auth-choice xiaomi-token-plan-sgp --xiaomi-token-plan-api-key "$XIAOMI_TOKEN_PLAN_API_KEY"
```

--------------------------------

### Automated OpenClaw Installation via Shelley

Source: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/main/docs/install/exe-dev.md

Use this prompt with the Shelley agent to automate the installation, Nginx configuration, and initial setup of OpenClaw on an exe.dev VM.

```text
Set up OpenClaw (https://docs.openclaw.ai/install) on this VM. Use the non-interactive and accept-risk flags for openclaw onboarding. Add the supplied auth or token as needed. Configure nginx to forward from the default port 18789 to the root location on the default enabled site config, making sure to enable Websocket support. Pairing is done by "openclaw devices list" and "openclaw devices approve <request id>". Make sure the dashboard shows that OpenClaw's health is OK. exe.dev handles forwarding from port 8000 to port 80/443 and HTTPS for us, so the final "reachable" should be <vm-name>.exe.xyz, without port specification.
```

--------------------------------

### Defining a setup entry point

Source: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/main/docs/plugins/sdk-setup.md

Use setup-entry.ts to define a lightweight entry point for setup-related tasks, avoiding heavy runtime dependencies.

```typescript
// setup-entry.ts
import { defineSetupPluginEntry } from "openclaw/plugin-sdk/channel-core";
import { myChannelPlugin } from "./src/channel.js";

export default defineSetupPluginEntry(myChannelPlugin);
```

--------------------------------

### Non-interactive setup

Source: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/main/docs/providers/meta.md

Command for automated onboarding in non-interactive environments.

```bash
openclaw onboard --non-interactive --accept-risk \
  --mode local \
  --auth-choice meta-api-key \
  --meta-api-key "$MODEL_API_KEY"
```

--------------------------------

### AI-Evaluated Discretion Condition Example

Source: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/main/extensions/open-prose/skills/prose/compiler.md

This example demonstrates using discretion markers (`**...**`) for AI-evaluated conditions to guide session execution based on code analysis.

```prose
let analysis = session "Analyze the codebase"

if **the code has security vulnerabilities**:
  session "Fix security issues immediately"
    context: analysis
elif **the code has performance issues**:
  session "Optimize performance bottlenecks"
    context: analysis
else:
  session "Proceed with normal review"
    context: analysis
```

--------------------------------

### Install Exa plugin

Source: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/main/docs/tools/exa-search.md

Install the Exa plugin and restart the gateway to apply changes.

```bash
openclaw plugins install @openclaw/exa-plugin
openclaw gateway restart
```
